name: Pet Needs Panel
description: The care dashboard for the equipped pet: feeding, cleanliness, and play meters with action buttons that request care interactions. It is a projection and a remote control, not a simulation — the meters render pets.pet_companion's authoritative hunger and happiness state, and the buttons emit care-action requests that the training and care systems fulfill. Keeping state out of the panel is deliberate: a UI that caches its own copy of 'hunger' will eventually disagree with the pet, and every disagreement is a bug report. The panel also owns the at-a-glance warning affordance (a meter flashing at critical) but not the consequence of ignoring it — the pet's own systems decide what chronic neglect does. Unlike the human-scale social.needs_decay meters, pet needs here are few, visible, and player-driven: the pet does not feed itself, which is exactly what makes the care loop the player's job.

inputs.name: meterDefinitions
inputs.description: Meters to display: id, source output on the pet, critical threshold, and the care action that refills it. Data-driven so a pet with a 'grooming' meter needs no panel code change.

inputs.name: warningThreshold
inputs.description: Meter level below which the warning affordance shows. Low enough to give the player time to act, high enough that the warning is not permanent decoration.

inputs.name: careActionCooldownSeconds
inputs.description: Minimum interval between accepted care actions. Prevents feed-spam from trivializing the loop and gives animations room to play.

outputs.name: meterLevels
outputs.description: Current displayed level per meter, read from the pet each tick rather than stored.

outputs.name: activeWarnings
outputs.description: Meter ids currently below the warning threshold, so the HUD badge and the panel never compute the warning condition twice.
